newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close just below year high.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close just below year high.

text.p: French shares closed sharply higher on Tuesday, but below the year's highs, on the back of a rally in bonds and market relief over Russian president Boris Yeltsin's heart surgery, dealers said.
They also noted Wall Street was rising sharply in the conviction that Bill Clinton will carry the presidential elections today.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 45.17 points or 2.11 percent at 2,187.32 while the CAC-40 futures contract was up 46 at 2,193. The year high for the CAC-40 stands at 2,190.76.
Volume was six billion francs of which 3.97 billion on CAC-40 shares.

Rhone-Poulenc hit a year high, up 2.79 percent at 154.70 francs on back of interview with chairman Jean-Rene Fourtou in Financial Times, promising a rise in the share price in the next few years. Analysts also note Rhone-Poulenc Rorer announced good results with its Campto anti-cancer drug.
UAP continued to rise on takeover speculation for third running day. Share up 3.61 percent at 111.90 francs. UAP denied rumours of closer ties with Axa.
Valeo closed 2.64 percent lower at 302.60 after CGIP bought a 20 percent stake from Cerus. Valeo head Noel Goutard said there would be no change in direction.
